questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get away from them. Trying to get back at them makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A series of curves is ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes very slippery when wet.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Do all of these things to drive safely in the dark.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop right away. Move your car out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop serious bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: You feel angry about something that happened at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Turn up the radio so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to calm down.
Take a few minutes to relax before you drive home.
Stop for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to relax before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving when emotional is dangerous for you and others.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down so you can safely handle these curves.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level?

options.text: Give your body time to break down the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol or make you sober. They might help you stay awake, but they do not change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol while taking drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can strengthen the effects of both. It is not safe to drive after using either one, and it is even more dangerous to use them together.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Keep extra space between your vehicle and theirs.
Understand that the driver is not paying full attention to the road.
Do not drive the same way.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. Never look at passengers, search for things in your car, read, sightsee, or daydream. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space. Distracted drivers are more likely to cause accidents.

questions.question: Where should you keep your vehicle inspection certificate?

options.text: In a safe place at home.
It will be sent to you by the County Department of Finance.

questions.explanation: All vehicles on public roads must have an official inspection once a year. You will receive two copies of the inspection certificate. One copy must stay in your vehicle at all times.

questions.question: When driving on any public street or highway, what must you have?

options.text: Show your driver license to police if they ask.
Carry your driver license with you.

questions.explanation: You must have a valid driver license with you at all times when driving. You must show it to a police officer when asked.

questions.question: What is required when you take a road test for a driver license?

options.text: The vehicle must be safe and have no defects.
A licensed driver must drive you to the test.

questions.explanation: You must bring a licensed driver with you to the test. You must provide a safe vehicle with a current inspection certificate and active insurance. Fix any safety problems before the test.

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals. However, when a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving right away.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass when there is oncoming traffic, your view is blocked by a hill or curve, at an intersection, at railroad crossings, on bridges, or in no-passing zones. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: When towing a trailer, it must have:

options.text: Properly mounted wheels covered with fenders or mud guards.

questions.explanation: Trailer wheels must be properly mounted, lubricated, and covered with fenders or mud guards. Tires must be in good condition and properly inflated. The trailer must have the right lights and reflectors.

questions.question: To drive a heavy truck in Hawaii, you must:

options.text: Have a valid driver license for that type of vehicle.
Drive the truck only on truck routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a valid driver license for that type of vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must have a valid license for the type of vehicle you want to drive. See the Hawaii Drivers Manual for information about all license types.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Which of these items can you add to your private vehicle?

options.text: A blue light that shows outside the vehicle
A bell, exhaust whistle, or siren

questions.explanation: You cannot add a bell, exhaust whistle, or siren to your vehicle. You cannot add a red light that shows from the front or a blue light that shows outside. You cannot add a muffler cut-out, bypass, or any muffler that makes more noise than the original.

questions.question: You cannot pass another vehicle:
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass at hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.

questions.question: When towing a trailer or house trailer, you should:

options.text: Have someone ride in the trailer to keep the load steady.
Allow only adults to ride in the trailer.
Never allow anyone to ride in the trailer.
Allow people to ride in house trailers only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never allow anyone to ride in the trailer.
questions.explanation: No one should ride in any type of trailer. It is against the law.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and help drivers drive safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey posted speed limits, and allow plenty of travel time.

questions.question: Alcohol can affect you in which of these ways?

options.text: It gives you a feeling of false confidence.
It impairs your ability to think.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment, self-control, and coordination. It slows your reaction time and impairs your vision and distance judgment. You may also feel overly confident.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks:

options.text: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles.
Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Require less time to pass on an incline than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large, they need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is probably:

options.text: A person involved with a traffic study.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, as they are blind.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: Directed to do so by a flagger.
It is controlled by a stop sign.
Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger directs you to, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to vehicles still in the intersection. You may continue, but be ready to slow down and stop if the light changes.
